title: UPLC-MS/MS Detection of Metabolites in Grass Carp Tissues
author: Honghao Zhao
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.smgec3w

steps.title: Sample Preparation and Extraction
steps.instruction: Extract metabolites from grass carp white muscle and gonadal tissues.

substeps.instruction: Collect samples from 5 individuals per replicate (approximately 25 mg per sample).
Place samples of 5 tails into an EP tube.
Add 800 μL of an ice-cold mixture of methanol and water (1:1 ratio) and two steel balls to each tube.
Homogenize tissues using a TissueLyser at 60 Hz for 5 minutes.
Centrifuge at 25000 g for 10 minutes at 4 °C.
Collect 300 μL of supernatant for LC-MS injection.

steps.title: UPLC Chromatographic Separation
steps.instruction: Perform reversed phase separation using an Ultimate 2777C UPLC system.

substeps.instruction: Equip the system with an ACQUITY UPLC BEH C18 column (100 mm * 2.1 mm, 1.7 μm).
Set the column oven temperature to 50 °C.
Prepare mobile phases: Solvent A (water + 0.1% formic acid) and Solvent B (acetonitrile + 0.1% formic acid).
Set the flow rate to 0.4 ml/min and injection volume to 10 μL.
Apply the following gradient elution: 0-2 min (100% A); 2-11 min (0% to 100% B); 11-13 min (100% B); 13-15 min (0% to 100% A).

steps.title: Mass Spectrometry Acquisition
steps.instruction: Analyze eluents using a SYNAPT G2-XS QTOF mass spectrometer with electrospray ionization.

substeps.instruction: Set capillary voltages to 2.0 kV (positive mode) and 1.0 kV (negative mode).
Set cone voltages to 40 V for both modes.
Acquire data in Centroid MSE mode with a TOF mass scan range of 50 m/z to 1200 m/z and a scan time of 0.2 seconds.
Fragment precursors using 20-40 eV for MS/MS detection.
Calibrate mass accuracy by acquiring the MS signal every 3 seconds.

steps.title: Data Processing and Alignment
steps.instruction: Process raw data using Progenesis QI software (version 2.2).

substeps.instruction: Crop data to remove external standards.
Detect masses and build chromatograms using the Centroid mass detector and Chromatogram builder.
Deconvolute smoothed data using a noise amplitude algorithm and perform deisotoping.
Align chromatograms using a 0.01 m/z tolerance and 0.1 min RT-tolerance.
Search for sodium and ammonium adducts.
Export the compound identification list (molecular weight, name, statistical scores) as a .csv file.

steps.title: Statistical Analysis
steps.instruction: Perform univariate and multivariate data analysis using MetaboAnalyst 4.0.

substeps.instruction: Input peak intensity tables into the 'Statistical Analysis' module.
Normalize data using a pooled sample (QC) from the two experimental groups.
Apply log transformation and autoscaling for normalization.

steps.title: Compound Identification and Verification
steps.instruction: Verify candidate compounds by comparing molecular weights and MOL files against databases.

substeps.instruction: Search the METLIN batch Metabolite Search Database, KEGG, HMDB, and ChemSpider.
Retrieve molecular and structural formulas of candidate compounds.
Confirm identifications via MS/MS scans for characteristic ions and fragmentation patterns.
